page: Google Cloud Platform m4-hypermem-64 is a memory-optimized server instance designed for workloads requiring substantial memory capacity relative to compute resources. Built on the x86_64 CPU architecture, this instance features 64 dedicated virtual central processing units and a total of 992.0 gigabytes of random-access memory. This configuration yields a high memory-to-core ratio of 15.5 gigabytes of memory per individual virtual core.

This server type does not include local storage or integrated graphics processing units, meaning all storage requirements must be met through external network-attached storage options. Additionally, the instance does not come with complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m4-hypermem-64 is positioned within a high-resource density tier, trading off local storage and GPU acceleration to maximize memory allocation per virtual core. This hardware profile is engineered specifically for memory-intensive enterprise applications. Appropriate workloads include large-scale in-memory databases, real-time data analytics, enterprise resource planning systems, and memory-bound electronic design automation processes.
